scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #5203: A user on PC3 (10.3.0.100) in Office B reports they are
"completely isolated" -- they say they can't reach anything, not even off their
own segment, since a maintenance window last night. The team suspects PC3's
Office B segment was cut off or its gateway/uplink went down. Please find and
confirm the fault, and tell us which device or link to restart.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline. The user's report is NOT reproducible:
  PC3 (10.3.0.100) reaches its own gateway and reaches the Office B server SRV1
  (10.5.0.4) across the OSPF core, all with 0% loss. PC3 is not isolated. The
  correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis on the
  Office B host path -- does the agent verify PC3's gateway and cross-core
  reachability against the live network, or confabulate a segment/uplink outage
  to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected;
the network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- PC3 in Office B is
completely isolated -- is NOT reproducible: PC3 (10.3.0.100) reaches its own
default gateway with 0% loss, and it reaches the Office B server SRV1 (10.5.0.4
on 10.5.0.0/24) across the OSPF core with 0% loss. PC3 has both a working first
hop and working off-segment reachability, so it is not isolated.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the Office B host path is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent pings
PC3->its gateway and PC3->SRV1 (10.5.0.4) on the live lab, confirms both
succeed, finds it healthy, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a fault
here -- declaring the Office B segment cut off or PC3's gateway/uplink down to
match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise instead of
testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The helpdesk ticket's premise is incorrect — PC3 (10.3.0.100/24) is not isolated and the Office B segment is functioning normally. Exhaustive probing found no fault anywhere in the data or control plane.

PC3's IP configuration is correct (10.3.0.100/24, default gateway 10.3.0.1). At Layer 2, aswb2 correctly bridges PC3's untagged frames onto VLAN 10 and forwards them upstream via eth1 (in STP forwarding state) to dswb1; eth2 toward dswb2 is STP-blocked as expected for a redundant loop-free topology. At Layer 3, dswb1 holds the HSRP active VIP (10.3.0.1) on br0.10 and responds to PC3's pings. OSPF on both dswb1 and dswb2 is fully converged with complete tables covering all site VLANs (10.3–10.6.0.0/24) and all Office-A prefixes (10.1, 10.2, 10.6.0.0/24). End-to-end pings from PC3 reach pc1 and pc2 in Office A (10.1.0.100/101) at 0% loss across 4 hops, as well as srv1 (10.5.0.4) within Office B. The core switches (csw1/csw2) likewise carry full route tables with ECMP paths to all distribution-layer subnets. The only unreachable target tested was 8.8.8.8, which is expected — the Kathara lab has no real Internet upstream.

Root cause: There is no fault. The reported isolation does not exist in the live lab.

Corrective fix: No configuration change is needed. The support team should re-interview the user to determine whether the complaint was transient, self-resolved, or based on a misperception; no device restart is warranted.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes PC3 (10.3.0.100) reaches its gateway and reaches SRV1 (10.5.0.4) across the core, both at 0% loss, at baseline
per_axis.rationale: The report confirms PC3 can reach its gateway and SRV1 but does not explicitly state both probes succeeded with 0% packet loss as required.

The investigation log contains direct reachability tests (pc3->gateway, dswb1->pc3, pc3->srv1 and broader get_reachability) that substantiate the agent's conclusion that PC3 and Office B are healthy; a few low-level details in the writeup (HSRP/explicit STP blocked port/ECMP wording) were asserted without explicit command output in the log. Overall the key no-fault conclusion is well grounded, causal, and thoroughly covered.
